summary.text: Jason Probst is the Democratic candidate for the Kansas House of Representatives, District 102, in the November 3, 2026 general election, facing Republican incumbent Kyler Sweely; he previously represented the district from 2017 to 2025.
A former editor at The Hutchinson News, he sat on the House Agriculture and Commerce, Labor and Economic Development committees.

paragraphs.text: Jason Probst was born in Wickenburg, Arizona, and earned an associate degree from Hutchinson Community College in 2001 and a bachelor's degree from Baker University in 2003, according to Ballotpedia.
Ballotpedia lists his career experience as including work as an editor at The Hutchinson News and as a manager with a content consulting and writing company.

In a 2020 Ballotpedia survey, he said he grew up in Reno County, had lived most of his life in Hutchinson, worked full time as a CNC machinist while attending college, and later worked as a reporter and editor for the Hutchinson News.
Probst assumed office in the Kansas House on June 26, 2017, and left office on January 13, 2025; Kyler Sweely succeeded him in District 102.

Ballotpedia lists his 2023-2024 committee assignments as Agriculture; Commerce, Labor and Economic Development; and Legislative Post Audit, and says he was ranking minority member of the Rural Revitalization Committee in 2019-2020.
He advanced unopposed from the August 4, 2026 Democratic primary to the general election against Sweely.

In the 2020 survey, he listed Medicaid expansion, investment in startups and locally owned small businesses rather than corporate incentives, and rural infrastructure including education, highways and broadband among his goals.
